chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from his father from Abd al-Rahman b. Salim from al-Mufaddal from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

When a servant stands before his Lord, exalted be His majesty, in the middle of the night, prays four units of prayer deep into a dark night, then prostrates a prostration of gratitude after completing his prayer, and says 'Whatever Allah wills, whatever Allah wills' one hundred times, Allah, exalted be His majesty, calls to him from above him: 'O My servant! How long will you say: Whatever Allah wills, whatever Allah wills! I am your Lord, and the will is Mine. I have willed the fulfillment of your need, so ask Me for whatever you wish.'

key_terms.فَسَلْنِي مَا شِئْتَ: So ask Me whatever you wish

ai.seo_question: What happens when you say 'ma sha Allah' 100 times after night prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) describes a powerful night worship practice: when a servant stands before Allah at midnight, prays four units in the darkness, performs a gratitude prostration, and repeats 'Whatever Allah wills' one hundred times, Allah Himself responds from above with a direct divine address. Allah tells the servant to stop deferring and simply ask, because He has already willed to fulfill the servant's need. This hadith was understood by the original audience as instruction on the etiquette of tahajjud prayer and the intimate divine-servant dialogue that occurs during the stillest hours of night.
